Minutes of the Riverside Allotment Society annual meeting. The meeting opened at the community hall with nineteen members present and apologies from four others. The chair thanked the volunteers who repaired the north fence after the winter storms, and noted that the water butts donated by the hardware shop on Mill Lane have now been installed on every second plot. The treasurer reported that membership fees covered the insurance renewal and most of the seed order, but that the shed roof will need replacing within two years. Several members raised the problem of bindweed spreading from the vacant plots along the railway side, and it was agreed that a work party would clear them before the end of April. There was a long discussion about whether to allow bees on the site. Some members were enthusiastic, citing better pollination for the fruit trees; others were worried about children using the path to the playground. No decision was reached and the committee will ask the council for guidance. The compost bays will be rebuilt using pallets from the builders' yard, and anyone with a trailer is asked to help. The summer produce show will again be judged by the retired headteacher who judged it last year, and categories for the largest marrow and the best jam will stay. Under any other business, a member asked whether the gate code could be changed more often, since a number of people who no longer hold plots still seem to know it. The secretary agreed to change it quarterly. Finally, the society elected Margaret Okafor as its new chair, replacing Tom Wendell, who stepped down after six years. The annual fee for next season was set at 42 pounds per full plot. The next general meeting will be held on 14 October 2026 at 7:30 pm in the same hall. The meeting closed with thanks to the tea rota and a reminder that plot inspections begin in June.
